defects.title: The minimum objective is not imposed when the objective coefficient is not 1
defects.trigger: a model whose objective coefficient is not exactly 1 (toy model with model.c = [0; 0; 0; 2]), randomObjFBASol(model, {'max', 0.9}); the same with a third entry minObjValue
defects.observed: (R2025a, gurobi, 2026-11-25) with rng(1), 10 of 20 calls return EX_B below 0.9 * 10 = 9 (0 of 20 with model.c(4) = 1); lines 32 and 34 bound only reactions with model.c == 1, so no reaction is bounded
defects.expected: every returned solution reaches at least minObjFrac times the optimum (or minObjValue), as the help text says, for any objective vector .c

notes: Reproduction: model = createModel({'EX_A';'R1';'R2';'EX_B'}, {'EX_A';'R1';'R2';'EX_B'}, {' -> A';'A -> B';'A -> B';'B -> '}, 'lowerBoundList', [0 0 0 0], 'upperBoundList', [10 1000 1000 1000]); model = changeObjective(model, 'EX_B'); model.c(4) = 2; rng(1); n = 0; for k = 1:20, x0 = randomObjFBASol(model, {'max', 0.9}); n = n + (x0(4) < 9 - 1e-6); end; disp(n)  % prints 10 (0 with model.c(4) = 1). Reach: optimizeCbModelNLP uses randomObjFBASol as its default initFunction (feval of the initFunction name; default initArgs {osenseStr, 0.5, 0.5*solOpt.f}), so every optimizeCbModelNLP call without another initFunction reaches it; whether only models with c ~= 1 on the objective count (input-dependent) is for the lead.
confirmed_by: lead, 2026-11-25: code read (lines 32 and 34 constrain only reactions with c == 1 exactly, so another coefficient drops the minimum objective fraction silently); writer reproduced in MATLAB; default reach
